A day of immense pride, both personal and familial.

This evening, I was honoured to be conferred my Master’s in Construction Law and Dispute Resolution from King’s College London at the Royal Festival Hall. A particular highlight was wearing the iconic white robes of The Dickson Poon School of Law—designed for King’s by the legendary Dame Vivienne Westwood. King's College London law graduates wear black robes with white elements because it's a blend of traditional legal attire, symbolising authority (black) and purity (white), and King's own modern design, adopted after gaining degree powers in 2007, linking to medieval roots while distinguishing its unique academic dress. The black robe's history stems from 17th-century mourning orders for Queen Mary II, which lawyers adopted for its solemnity and professional distinction, while the white represents fairness and transparency in justice. 

Beyond history and symbolism the day was made infinitely more special by having my wonderful wife and three daughters there to share it. Having my biggest supporters in the audience meant the world. Thank you for cheering on your very proud dad. I am also immensely grateful to all my fellow class mates and all those in the graduate year of 2026 who gave me a standing ovation, it all meant so much!

As one chapter closes, another exciting one begins. I am thrilled to continue my journey with King’s, now stepping into new roles as a Scholar and Ambassador with King’s Business School as I undertake an executive MBA.

My sincere thanks also go to the brilliant tutors and professors at King’s. The academic rigour and innovative spirit they instil have been instrumental, enabling me to add tangible value every day in my cross service-line work at Egis to drive growth and partnership in regulated nuclear, water, energy transmission, environment and defence.

This achievement stands at the intersection of incredible support and new opportunity and aiming to continue to add immense value to the construction sector and Egis. Onwards!

📣 Exciting news! Kingsley Clarke, Head of SCF Frameworks (South West) has been appointed as The National Association of Construction Framework's (NACF’s) new chair.

SCF is a founder member of NACF and Kingsley will become the third chair in NACF’s 11-year history, two of whom were part of the SCF team.
 
His leadership will help guide NACF as it continues to champion collaborative frameworks, value-led procurement, and sustainable delivery across the UK construction sector.

🗣️ Kingsley said:

“It is groups like this feeding into Local Government decisions, whether that be on delivering new homes or tackling the skills/labour shortage, that can make the difference and the case for better thought-out projects and construction procurement.

“I’m excited to make a difference and demonstrate the power of construction frameworks, designed by the public sector for the public sector.
 
“I’d like to thank John Simons, who has successfully chaired the group since Keith Heard’s retirement, leading the group through a challenging time in the construction industry, enabling best practice to be shared with the public sector.”

#Construction #Frameworks #Leadership #Collaboration #NACF

We've increased automation, digitisation, and addressed many industry issues including measures to eliminate labour abuse, unfair payment practices, and embracing the use of Should Cost Models to ensure sustainable project delivery.

text:
Like many of you, I’ve recently read the news about ISG entering administration, and I wanted to reach out to express my solidarity during this difficult time. The news of the company’s collapse and the redundancies affecting so many of us is deeply saddening.
 
It’s been a privilege to work alongside such talented individuals and I’ve appreciated every moment of collaboration. While this news brings a lot of uncertainty, I’m confident that the skills and dedication you’ve all shown will carry you forward to new and exciting opportunities.
 
Let’s stay connected on LinkedIn, and I hope we can cross paths again in the near future.
 
Wishing everyone all the best during this transition.

After the tragic news of ISG last night and this morning, its heart breaking to see many people that we have worked with on projects and collaborated with now looking for new roles.

text:
Turned away from football as a child because of his rare disability, procurement and supply chain manager Sam Nunn persisted. 🗨️ “Never give up… and don’t let anyone bring you down,” he would say.  

It’s an attitude that would see him go on to compete for semi-professional amputee football teams at Wimbledon, Southend United and Ipswich Town. ⚽

After hanging up his boots in 2008, the Olympics and Paralympics were on the horizon. Sam wondered if there was another competitive sport out there for him. There was. 

Clay pigeon shooting was Sam’s next target – and he won Clay Pigeon Shooting (CPSA) Disabled Shooter of the Year Award on two occasions, alongside the English Open Champion in 2014. 🏅

Sam’s story is one of determination and overcoming adversity. A message that rings true today with the opening ceremony of the Paralympics. Like Sam, the incredible male and female athletes remind us of the importance of inclusivity. In Sam’s own words: “There’s something out there for everyone.” 💛

Read Sam’s story here 👇
https://ow.ly/Rg1I50T8HgY

text:
ISG has returned to Cambridge to deliver its latest low carbon retrofit project – this time for The Crown Estate at the Cambridge Business Park. Cambridge is already home to a global exemplar deep office retrofit project, following ISG’s successful delivery of the multi-award winning Entopia Building for the Cambridge Institute for Sustainability Leadership (CISL).

For the Crown Estate, ISG conducted a comprehensive de-carbonisation assessment survey of the Cambridge Business Park estates. The second phase of the programme saw the contractor deliver a smart Low Carbon Retrofit upgrade, focusing on building performance enhancements, alongside significant energy reduction measures to slash carbon emissions and reduce operational running costs.  

🗨️ Lee Phillips, Managing Director of ISG said: “As the race to decarbonise property assets accelerates, portfolio owners are increasingly seeking out contractors that can provide a comprehensive service offer from consultancy, delivery through to end-user monitoring and optimisation.”
